sprint: Magic Publish — per-object staging + the spec'd arrival motion, as one change. Reported: "talking about magic publish its not looking like a movie. it is just looking like animated page turn". Diagnosed as two independent causes that both want the same missing piece — stages must record WHICH object arrived. (a) Motion invisible: RISE_PX=14 on a 1920-tall frame is 0.73% against the spec's own ~2%, RISE_SETTLE=0.45 spends the entire lift by t≈0.181 when the incoming frame is still under half-visible, and word steps use 'draw' → paintWash → zero movement; meanwhile the page turn between pages is a 520ms sweeping leaf with bow, highlight band and cast shadow, so the only thing that visibly moved WAS the page turn. (b) Staging collapses: two or three pictures produced the SAME three frames as one, every picture arriving simultaneously.
task:
PER-OBJECT STAGING (js/magicReveal.js). The Artwork and Decorations beats no longer arrive as one lump. New enumerators (_stickerKey/_placeIndex/_artworkArrivals/_decorationArrivals) list what a beat will bring, each keyed by the id that object carries in SlideRenderer's OWN render tree — Places resolve to 'image-holder' (index 0) or 'image-place-N', stickers to st.id, scene elements to el.id — so the caller can look the object up rather than guess. _arrivalSteps then turns a list of n arrivals into up to MAX_ARRIVALS_PER_GROUP=4 frames: n=1..4 give one object per frame; n=7 gives four frames where the first three name one object each and the last brings the remainder and honestly names NOTHING. Every stage carries `arrivalId` — the id when exactly one object arrived, null when the frame is not about a single object (the blank page, the World's furniture, a grouped remainder), and the caller falls back to the whole-frame crossfade, which is the honest reading. Partial staging is real rather than cosmetic: _applyArtwork/_applyDecorations take a shown-set (null = the whole beat, empty = none, populated = partial) and _stageSlide threads it through, with the partial artwork case building a FRESH place map (Object.assign({}, slide._placeImages||{})) before deleting keys, because _cloneSlide is a shallow Object.assign and clone._placeImages would otherwise be the caller's own object. The no-mutation guarantee holds: the caller's _placeImages, image and _magicSuppressPlaceholders are all untouched, and the final stage is still the caller's own slide.

THE SPEC'D ARRIVAL MOTION (js/reelComposer.js). New 'arrival' transition beside page-turn/wash/rise/draw: ARRIVAL_MS=560, ARRIVAL_RISE_PX=38 (~2% of 1920 — the spec's own figure, against rise's 14), ARRIVAL_START_SCALE=0.94, ARRIVAL_OVERSHOOT=1.04, ARRIVAL_PEAK_AT=0.62, ARRIVAL_CLIP_PAD=0.08. _arrivalScale(p) takes RAW progress (so a caller cannot double-ease it) and runs grow → overshoot → settle. paintArrival crossfades everything OUTSIDE the arriving object's rect via an evenodd two-rect clip — so the rest of the page is pixel-identical to a plain crossfade and does not move at all — while INSIDE a padded clip it scales and lifts the incoming frame about that rect's own centre. Without a usable rect it degrades to paintRise, exactly. One collision resolved rather than papered over: paintArrival wants ~38px and paintRise must keep 14, so compose()'s risePx default changed RISE_PX → null and each painter falls back to its own constant (paintRise already read `typeof risePx==='number'?risePx:RISE_PX`, so null correctly falls through); an explicit opts.risePx still overrides both, and every existing caller is byte-identical.

JOINING THE TWO (js/storyDestinations.js). MagicReveal names WHICH object arrived; SlideRenderer's render tree knows WHERE it is, in the slide's own logical pixels. _magicFrameMap reproduces _fitCompositeInto's own contain-fit centred arithmetic (which also gives the right answer on the fast path, where scale is 1 and both offsets are 0, so there is no branch), _magicArrivalRect maps the object's bbox into output-frame pixels, and _magicTransition gained a fourth argument: an object frame gets 'arrival' when a rect resolved and 'rise' when it did not. THE FINISHED FRAME'S TREE WAS THE ONE REAL PROBLEM: encodePage's finished stage reuses the pipeline's own canvas and skips _renderSlideInto, so by the time the loop reaches it getSceneElements() describes stage n-2. Re-rendering the finished page purely to refresh the tree (~65ms/page) was rejected; instead the tree is snapshotted at the TOP of encodePage, where PublishStudio's own createCanvas → renderPage → encodePage order means it already describes the finished page and is free. Every other stage reads the tree straight after its own render, so a rect always describes the frame it is attached to. A stage without a slide is skipped, so the transition tag uses frames.length rather than the loop index.

ONE DEFECT FOUND BY INSPECTION RATHER THAN BY A FAILING TEST: fitToBudget hands back the same stage objects, so `arrivalId` survived trimming — but a kept frame whose predecessor was dropped now brings everything the dropped stages would have, while still claiming one object. Reachable in practice: MAGIC_MAX_FRAMES=48 gives a 4-page story 12 frames per page, and a page with world + 2 places + 2 decorations + 8 words is 14 stages. Fixed with gap detection (idx-prev>1) that pushes a COPY with arrivalId:null, never editing the caller's own objects.

Verified 48/48 via a new magic_arrival_verify suite across seven sections, on a fixture theme that authors TWO Places so the render tree genuinely yields 'image-holder' and 'image-place-2': A proves two/three Places give two/three frames in Place order and seven decorations cap at four with the last honestly null; B proves a partial stage shows P1 and not yet P2, suppresses the authoring placeholder, writes to its own place map, and leaves the caller's slide untouched; C proves a tight budget keeps the ends AND nulls the claims it can no longer support while an untrimmed list hands back the very same objects; D measures the motion rather than eyeballing it — the lift is 30-45px, the scale starts under 1 and overshoots past it, the object is genuinely WIDER at ARRIVAL_PEAK_AT than at t=1 and settles within 2px of its own width, and outside the rect the frame is pixel-identical to paintWash at six sample points; E proves the rect resolves to real frame pixels — a 4:5 page letterboxes with scale 1 and oy 285, and Place 1 lands at exactly {x:64.8, y:420, w:432, h:405}, within 1px of getPlaceRects mapped through the frame map; F publishes end to end and reads EBML magic 1a45dfa3 off the blob's own first four bytes rather than inferring it from the UI; G confirms zero page errors. ONE TEST-METHODOLOGY BUG, disclosed and not an app bug: E8/E9 first compared the whole FRAME object against the expected rect (the app's own value was already exactly right), fixed to read frame.arrivalRect. ONE STALE ASSERTION UPDATED as the intended and disclosed consequence of this ship rather than a regression: magic_m4's G4 required object frames to be 'rise', which is precisely what this change replaces — split into G4a (a word frame draws, an object frame arrives or rises, never the other way round and never a page turn) and G4b (the arrival path is genuinely live, not merely permitted). Regression: magic_m1 32/32, m2 33/33, m3 32/32, m4 42/42, m5 43/43, m6 35/35, m7 38/38, m8 47/47, m9 21/21, reel 15/15, reel_backdrop 10/10, reel_pageturn 12/12, voice 16/16, voice_note 22/22, both goldenBuilds PASS. renderer/slideRenderer.js is untouched, so the Museum Gallery canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship; js/publishStudio.js needed no change (payloads are opaque to it) and js/magicStrip.js needed none either (selectFrames dedupes by kind keeping the last, so it still picks the all-pictures-present frame, which is the right still).
